cards.front: The CAM requires four features: (1) acute onset/fluctuating course AND (2) [___], PLUS either (3) disorganised thinking OR (4) altered level of consciousness. Features 1 and 2 are both mandatory.
cards.context:
The CAM has a sensitivity of 94-100% and specificity of 90-95% when administered by trained assessors.

Inattention is tested at the bedside by asking the patient to recite months backwards, spell WORLD backwards, or perform serial 7s.

cards.front: In biopsychosocial formulation, [___] factors are proximal triggers that convert predisposing vulnerability into an acute episode, answering 'Why now?'
cards.context: Distinguishing them from predisposing (distal vulnerability) and perpetuating (maintaining) factors guides both acute management and long-term treatment planning.
